note: Hand-written, language-neutral. The declared home of every HTTP name that crosses a process boundary in this platform (ADR-0036, C-04). Read by txnet-backend/shared-core/src/lib/http/wire.contract.spec.ts, by auth-handler/internal/api/handlers/headers_contract_test.go, and by tools/contracts.py. Change a value here and every consumer goes red until it agrees. Unlike contracts/jwt/ts-to-go.json this file is NOT generated: Traefik reads YAML and has no toolchain that could consume a generated Go or TypeScript file, so the source has to be a format all three sides read.

identityHeaders.note: Written by auth-handler onto a 2xx from /validate, forwarded by Traefik (authResponseHeaders) and stripped from the inbound request (strip-fake-headers). Canonical casing is the spelling auth-handler writes; HTTP header names are case-insensitive on the wire, so a Node reader lowercases before indexing req.headers.

gateHeaders.note: Not an identity header: it says the gate ran and identified nobody (ADR-0031). Forwarded and stripped exactly like the identity set.

requestHeaders.note: Sent by a caller and read by a service. Declared lowercase because that is how Node exposes an inbound header name. The tenant header is not here: x-tenant-id and X-Tenant-Id are one case-insensitive name, so both directions use identityHeaders.tenantId.

proxyHeaders.note: Set by Traefik, not by anything in this repo, so there is no drift to prevent — recorded only so the codebase spells each one in exactly one place (C-04).

cookieLifetimesSec.note: Seconds, matching Max-Age and every TTL in the platform. The cookie and the token it carries are one lifetime: a cookie outliving its token is a browser that believes it is signed in and is refused on every refresh.

cookies.note: One name per cookie that crosses the browser boundary, and the one lifetime its Max-Age and its token TTL share. The options builder stays with the code that sets the cookie.
